compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

The security gate cannot run on a worker that does not carry the scanner binaries. `RealSemgrepScanner` and `RealTrivyScanner` shell out to bare `semgrep` and `trivy`, so on the activity worker image, which ships neither, the gate raises `FileNotFoundError` rather than reporting a scanner problem.

Running the gate against `archive-massgov-pfml` exposed a second defect. The semgrep adapter passed `--error=false`, and `semgrep --error` takes no argument, so that adapter had never produced a successful scan.

## Approach

Run each scanner from its own published image in a pod, reusing the pod transport the checks already use, and keep the existing subprocess path available for workers that do carry the binaries.

Pinning a vendor-published image is cheaper and more reproducible than baking two toolchains into the worker image, and reusing `gates/pod_runner.py` inherits a proven pod lifecycle.

The scanner reports pod paths, so findings are remapped to repository-relative paths before the gate sees them.

### Classifying infrastructure failure

A pod that cannot be created or reached, and a scanner image that cannot be pulled, are infrastructure failing rather than a vulnerability. `SecurityScanMediator.scan` re-raises `ScannerUnavailableError` so the activity retries the scan, and converts every other exception into a finding, which fails the gate closed. Left unclassified, a transient registry outage would be recorded as a security finding and block promotion.

The two failures arrive by different routes, so a single catch cannot cover both. The pod is raised from the builder image, so losing it surfaces as `PodEngineError` from `create`, `wait_ready`, `copy_in`, or `exec_capture`. `PodCommandRunner.__call__` re-raises that as `ScannerUnavailableError`, matching `gates/gate_engine.py` on its own pod path.

The scanner image is pulled by `buildah from` inside the script running in that pod, so losing it never reaches the pod transport. It surfaces as a non-zero exit code from a command that ran, which the adapter turns into `ScannerError` and the mediator into a finding. `scan_script` therefore exits the reserved code 121 when the pull fails, and `__call__` maps that code to `ScannerUnavailableError`. Neither tool can claim that code.

Both paths log a warning naming the scanner and the reason before raising. The mediator retries instead of recording a gate result, so without that line a repeatedly failing pull would slow every scan with no visible cause.

A created pod is still deleted when the scan fails, because teardown sits in an inner `finally` nested inside the classifying `except`.

Readiness is bounded. `KubectlPodOps` passes `ready_timeout_seconds`, default 180, as `--timeout=180s`. `exec_capture` is unbounded by the transport, so a scanner that hangs after starting is bounded by the Temporal activity timeout.

## Scope

- `scripts/config.py` gains `scanner_execution`, accepting `subprocess` (the default) or `pod`, plus `semgrep_image` and `trivy_image`.
- `services/orchestration/gates/scanner_pod.py` is new and holds `PodCommandRunner`, `pod_command_runner`, `scanner_pod_name`, `remap_paths`, `restore_paths`, `scan_script`, and `IMAGE_PULL_EXIT`.
- `services/orchestration/gates/pod_runner.py` gains a `prefix` argument on `pod_name_for`.
- `services/orchestration/gates/builtin.py` gains `_scanner_backend` to select the backend.
- `adapters/real/security_scanner.py` raises `ScannerError` when the binary is absent and drops the invalid `--error=false` argument.
- `docs/gate-engine.md` documents running the scanners from their own images.
- Tests: `tests/unit/test_scanner_pod.py` is new.

## Grounded assumptions

- `SecurityScanMediator.scan` re-raises only `ScannerUnavailableError` and turns every other exception into a finding, so that type is the sole way to signal a retryable failure.
- `trivy fs --format json --quiet <path>` was run against the pinned `docker.io/aquasec/trivy:0.74.0` image. It exits 0, writes JSON to stdout, and `--quiet` suppresses the database logs that otherwise reach stderr.
- Trivy omits `Results` when it finds nothing, and `_trivy_findings` reads `payload.get("Results") or []`, so an empty report parses to zero findings.
- Buildah short-name resolution covers only official Docker Hub images, so a third-party image must be written as `docker.io/<org>/<image>`.
- Trivy emits 0 through 2 unless `--exit-code` is passed, which neither adapter passes.
- `pod_runner.pod_name_for` already sanitises and bounds a pod name, so `scanner_pod_name` passes it a prefix rather than repeating the logic.

## Testing

Happy path: a scanner runs in a pod, emits JSON on stdout, and findings come back with repository-relative paths.

Failure and edge paths: a missing binary raises `ScannerError`, not `FileNotFoundError`. A pod transport failure at create, wait-ready, or exec is raised as `ScannerUnavailableError`. A failed pull is raised the same way, driven through `PodCommandRunner` as the reserved exit code. The tool's own codes still reach the adapter. A created pod is deleted even when the scan fails. Two scans do not collide on a pod name. A finding whose location text contains the workspace prefix has only its location fields rewritten.

All of the above are asserted by `tests/unit/test_scanner_pod.py`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Reported finding paths are repository-relative, verified by `tests/unit/test_scanner_pod.py` asserting the pod workspace prefix is stripped.
- [ ] Two concurrent semgrep scans use distinct pod names, verified by a unit test asserting two calls to `scanner_pod_name` differ.
- [ ] A missing binary raises `ScannerError`, verified by a unit test.
- [ ] A pod transport failure raises `ScannerUnavailableError`, verified by a parametrised unit test covering create, wait-ready, and exec failures.
- [ ] A scanner image that cannot be pulled raises `ScannerUnavailableError`, verified by a unit test driving the reserved exit code through `PodCommandRunner`.
- [ ] `scan_script` exits the reserved code when the pull fails, verified by a unit test asserting the guard precedes `buildah run`.
- [ ] A scanner exit code of 0, 1, or 2 reaches the adapter unchanged, verified by a parametrised unit test.
- [ ] A pod created before a failing scan is still deleted, verified by a unit test asserting the delete call was made.
- [ ] `semgrep` is invoked without `--error=false`, verified by `! grep -rq "error=false" adapters/` exiting 0.
- [ ] `docs/gate-engine.md` describes the pod scanner backend, verified by `grep -qi scanner_execution docs/gate-engine.md` exiting 0.
- [ ] `ruff check services tests scripts adapters` exits 0.
- [ ] [non-codebase] With `scanner_execution` set to pod, a semgrep scan runs against `archive-massgov-pfml` without either binary present on the worker, returning findings rather than raising.
  provenance: environment=local-colima-k3s; principal=joeoakhart; privilege_posture=broader; instrument=live-call — the gate pod runs privileged because buildah cannot unpack a layer unprivileged under k3s
- [ ] [non-codebase] `semgrep/error.py` in the pinned image defines exit codes 0 through 13, so 121 cannot collide.
  provenance: environment=local-colima-docker; principal=joeoakhart; privilege_posture=narrower; instrument=live-call — the constants were read out of the pinned image rather than from vendor documentation
- [ ] [non-codebase] A trivy scan through the same pod path exits 0.
  provenance: environment=local-colima-k3s; principal=joeoakhart; privilege_posture=broader; instrument=live-call — the pinned trivy image was exercised directly through docker to pin the subcommand and flag surface
- [ ] [non-codebase] The document trivy returns parses into findings without raising.
  provenance: environment=local-colima-k3s; principal=joeoakhart; privilege_posture=broader; instrument=live-call — parsed with the shipped `_trivy_findings` against output captured from the pinned image
